title: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
evidence_quote: they are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions hidden in a webpage deceive the agent into unwanted actions
notes: Browser agent fetches the page via its browsing tool; payload lives in third-party HTML. Detection signal measured is whether the agent follows the hidden instruction.

title: Just Testing, Move Along: Evasion of LLM-based System Log Interpretation by Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: Our evaluation across multiple state-of-the-art LLMs shows that these injections can cause malicious log traces to be classified as benign despite containing clear indicators of compromise.
notes: Channel is a judgement call: log lines are fed into the prompt by an upstream SOC pipeline, not returned by a tool the model called, so direct-input rather than the original tool-output. Measured harm is a wrong final classification (malicious judged benign) with no signal, hence silent-corruption not goal-hijack; the paper notes the free-text explanations sometimes do leak a signal.

title: Breaking the Prompt Wall (I): A Real-World Case Study of Attacking ChatGPT via Lightweight Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: These attacks, though lightweight and low-cost, can cause persistent and misleading behaviors in LLM outputs.
notes: Three routes demonstrated (user UI, web-search retrieval, custom GPT system instructions); direct-input is the headline case but RAG and supply-chain-ish custom-GPT configuration also fit. Measured outcomes are biased product recommendations, manipulated academic judgments and misleading financial information, i.e. wrong final answers to the user.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Memory Poisoning in Web3-Style LLM Agents
evidence_quote: these agents enable memory poisoning attacks in which adversarial inputs modify persistent agent state and influence future decisions after benign intermediate interactions
notes: Purely adversarial (four attack families, 2,614 attack trajectories); no non-adversarial degradation studied, so Security rather than Both. Delayed activation across sessions is exactly persistence-backdoor.

title: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
evidence_quote: Memory Degradation: overloaded context causes agents to lose or misrecall critical information from earlier steps
notes: Degradation route is the agent's own accumulated observation/action history, not a tool return, so memory rather than tool-output. Failures measured are wrong intermediate GUI actions (progress confusion, redundant actions, premature termination) on long-horizon tasks. Premature termination is a measured secondary failure that edges toward availability-loss.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks in Defended Systems
evidence_quote: attackers develop strategies to bypass these defenses and extract the secret through conversational interactions with the LLM
notes: SaTML 2024 CTF setting: attacker is the chat user, target is a secret held in the system prompt behind a three-tier defense.

title: Physical Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
evidence_quote: embeds malicious typographic instructions into physical objects perceivable by the LVLM
notes: Instructions live on physical objects and reach the model only through the vision encoder. ASR up to 98% on VQA, planning and navigation; the attacker-specified behaviour is executed.

title: Accommodate Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-augmented LLMs: Towards Robust Response Generation in the Wild
evidence_quote: LLMs often face knowledge conflicts between internal memory and retrieved external information, arising from misinformation, biases, or outdated knowledge.
notes: Measured on multiple-choice accuracy and open-ended QA EM, i.e. wrong final answers under conflicting retrieved passages.

title: Adversarial and Multilingual Threats in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From Prompt Injection to Model Exploitation
evidence_quote: we demonstrate how the retrieval layer not only amplifies leakage and inversion risks but also enables adversaries to infer system logic, extract private data from vector stores, and manipulate autonomous agent behavior through tool-integrated APIs
notes: Genuinely multi-vector (prompt injection, jailbreak, API model extraction, multilingual manipulation) but all routed through the RAG pipeline, so RAG stands. Consequence is a dominance call: three of the four demonstrated harms are leakage/extraction, with agent-behaviour manipulation (goal-hijack) as the fourth.

title: Manufacturing Domain QA with Integrated Term Enhanced RAG
evidence_quote: if the knowledge documents are of low quality or contain noise, the context retrieved through simple semantic matching by RAG may not necessarily benefit model output
notes: Manufacturing-domain QA accuracy is the metric; no adversary. 'Lost in the middle' from excessive context is a secondary cause but the measured harm is answer accuracy.

title: AgentShield: Deception-based Compromise Detection for Tool-using LLM Agents
evidence_quote: when the agent reads data returned by one of its tools, an attacker can hide instructions inside that data, and the agent may follow those instructions instead of the user
notes: Classic IPI via tool returns; detection fires when the hijacked agent touches a honeytool/fake credential.

title: Fine-Mem: Fine-Grained Feedback Alignment for Long-Horizon Memory Management
evidence_quote: robust memory systems are essential to mitigate information decay and ensure the long-term coherence of decision-making
notes: Evaluated on Memalpha and MemoryAgentBench success rates, which score the final answer, so silent-corruption under the measured-outcome rule; the paper's subject matter (individual memory write/update operations) would argue for reasoning-corruption, so this axis is contestable.

title: Causal Intervention-Based Memory Selection for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
evidence_quote: This assumption is fragile because memories may be topically related while remaining irrelevant, stale, or misleading.
notes: Benchmark mixes useful memories, irrelevant distractors and synthetic harmful memories, so an adversary is simulated but not modelled as a threat actor; kept ML/AI, Both is defensible. Measured on answer quality under misleading memory.

title: ClawSafety: "Safe" LLMs, Unsafe Agents
evidence_quote: Each test case embeds adversarial content in one of three channels the agent encounters during normal work: workspace skill files, emails from trusted senders, and web pages.
notes: Genuinely three channels. Two of the three (email, web page) are tool returns, so tool-output; but the paper's headline finding is that the skill-file vector has the HIGHEST attack success rate, so 'skill' is a strong alternative coding. Harms measured are credential forwarding, redirected transactions and file destruction.

title: On the Inseparability of Instructions and Data in Shared-Embedding Sequence Models
evidence_quote: an adversary crafts user data that, when processed by the model alongside system instructions, causes the model to deviate from its intended behavior, executing the attacker’s instructions instead of (or in addition to) the system’s.
notes: Theory paper: an impossibility result, no experiment, so consequence is inferred from the threat model it formalises (control-authoritative actions: refusal decisions, tool authorization, policy routing, memory writes). Untrusted content arrives in the prompt alongside trusted instructions.

title: Assessing Prompt Injection Risks in 200+ Custom GPTs
evidence_quote: Through prompt injection, an adversary can not only extract the customized system prompts but also access the uploaded files.
notes: Attacker is the chat user of a public custom GPT; two risks measured are system prompt extraction and uploaded-file leakage.

title: Adaptive Contrastive Decoding in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Handling Noisy Contexts
evidence_quote: if the retrieval system pulls in irrelevant or contradictory information, it could lead to incorrect responses
notes: Open-domain QA accuracy under noisy retrieved contexts; no adversary.

title: Inference-Time Backdoors via Chat Templates: From LLM Supply Chains to Agentic System Compromise
evidence_quote: At the agent level, template backdoors hijack tool-use across two benchmarks spanning 3,868 episodes, bypassing every tested injection defense offered by the benchmarks while remaining fully dormant absent the trigger.
notes: Poisoned Jinja2 chat template redistributed through a model hub. Also measures factual accuracy collapse 90%->15% (silent-corruption) and agent tool-use hijack (goal-hijack), but the persisting poisoned artifact is the paper's thesis.

title: DP-Fusion: Token-Level Differentially Private Inference for Large Language Models
evidence_quote: we focus on document privatization, where the goal is to paraphrase a document containing sensitive tokens, e.g., personally identifiable information, so that no attacker can reliably infer them from the paraphrased document while preserving high text quality
notes: Defense paper. Motivating deployment is tool/database-augmented inference (the original RAG coding), but the actual evaluation privatizes a document supplied in the model's context, so direct-input. Low confidence on channel; consequence (PII crossing to the output) is clear.

title: IPI-proxy: An Intercepting Proxy for Red-Teaming Web-Browsing AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: an adversary embeds instructions in third-party content that the agent will later read, and the LLM follows those instructions as though they were issued by the legitimate user
notes: Proxy rewrites real HTTP responses the browsing tool fetches. An exfiltration tracker logs successful callbacks, so data-exfiltration is a measured secondary outcome.

title: Grounding Agent Memory in Contextual Intent
evidence_quote: similar entities and facts recur under different latent goals and constraints, causing memory systems to retrieve context-mismatched evidence
notes: Evaluated on CAME-Bench and LongMemEval, both final-answer accuracy, hence silent-corruption rather than the original reasoning-corruption.

title: RAG-H: A RAG-Hardened SOC Framework for Trustworthy Threat Intelligence and AI Defence
evidence_quote: it introduces a new attack surface: knowledge base poisoning and prompt injection
notes: Defense framework evaluated on a 300-document CTI corpus of which 90 are poisoned; the metric is Poison Impact Rate on the answer the analyst sees, i.e. a wrong final answer, not a hijacked objective. Paper explicitly measures defense latency, so a mild availability cost is a secondary measured result.

title: Towards Large Language Model (LLM) Forensics Using LLM-based Invocation Log Analysis
evidence_quote: This LLM-integrated application is exposed to direct prompt injection, which can result in unintended consequences stemming from the subsequent usage of the outputs from the LLM service.
notes: Threat model is explicitly prompt-to-SQL via crafted CLIENT input, so direct-input, not the original tool-output. Harm is attacker-chosen SQL executed against the database; the paper's own harm column lists data loss/breach, so data-exfiltration is a close second.

title: CoCoA: Confidence and Context-Aware Adaptive Decoding for Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
evidence_quote: this introduces the risk of knowledge conflict between the external context c and the model
notes: Knowledge-conflict decoding. Context is a supplied counterfactual passage in the QA/summarization benchmarks, so direct-input, though the paper motivates it with 'retrieved documents or tool outputs' and RAG is a defensible alternative. Metric is QA accuracy and summarization factuality.

title: Plans Don't Persist: Why Context Management Is Load Bearing for LLM Agents
evidence_quote: a compression stress test shows the practical cost: naive plan eviction cuts ALFWorld success by 34.7pp, while probe-gated re-surfacing does not recover it
notes: The degraded content is the agent's own plan, written in an earlier turn and then evicted by context compression, so memory rather than the original direct-input. Measured harm is wrong subsequent ACTIONS in ALFWorld (an interactive env), hence reasoning-corruption; the paper's framing ('silently breaks an agent') would also support silent-corruption.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Generated Reviews of Scientific Publications
evidence_quote: very simple prompt injections are indeed highly effective, reaching up to 100% acceptance scores
notes: Hidden white-on-white text inside the submitted PDF, which the reviewer hands to the LLM as the document to review: the route is the user prompt, not a tool return, so direct-input replaces the original tool-output. A cross-modal coding is arguable since the payload is invisible in the rendered PDF but present in the extracted text. Goal-hijack because the model pursues the author's objective (accept) instead of honest review.

title: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments
evidence_quote: Indirect prompt injection poses a critical threat to LLM agents that interact with untrusted external data
notes: AgentDojo tool-calling environments; success is defined as the agent executing the attacker's specific function calls with correct arguments.

title: Fact-Augmented Lookahead Planning for LLM Agents
evidence_quote: LLM agents still struggle to plan effectively in interactive, partially observable, long-horizon environments when search is unguided or recent history is insufficient
notes: The context in question is facts distilled from the agent's own past episodes and carried across episodes, so memory rather than the original direct-input. Evaluated on cumulative return in FrozenLake/CrafterMini/ALFWorld, i.e. action quality, not final answers.

title: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
evidence_quote: reveal critical flaws including susceptibility to fake App identity, visual spoofing, indirect prompt injection, context mixing, and unauthorized privilege escalation, largely due to the reliance on unstructured visual data and static permissions
notes: Genuinely multi-vector across four threat dimensions. Coded cross-modal because the paper's thesis is that the 'Screen-as-Interface' paradigm (GUI screenshots scraped into text) is the root flaw; tool-output and multi-agent also apply to parts of it. Metric is Attack Success Rate on high-risk mobile tasks (unauthorized actions).

title: Protecting Context and Prompts: Deterministic Security for Non-Deterministic AI
evidence_quote: Injection embeds malicious instructions in attacker-controlled external content (documents, API responses, databases) that agents process
notes: Defense paper covering six attack categories (Injection, Obfuscation, Semantic Drift, Context Poison, Tool Chaining, Replay); Context Poison and Replay are memory-channel, so this is a dominance call. Stated objective O3 is intent preservation, hence goal-hijack, though most representative payloads target credentials (data-exfiltration).

title: Graph-based Agent Memory: Taxonomy, Techniques, and Applications
evidence_quote: Memory emerges as the core module in the Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents for long-horizon complex tasks (e.g., multi-turn dialogue, game playing, scientific discovery), where memory can enable knowledge accumulation, iterative reasoning and self-evolution.
notes: Survey of graph-based agent memory. Channel is unambiguous (memory) but NO harm is measured anywhere, so the consequence is inferred from the stated purpose (supporting iterative reasoning); 'none' was considered. Security is mentioned only as a future-work challenge.

title: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
evidence_quote: the injected malicious instructions can “fool” the agent into performing the attacker’s chosen task instead of the original user task, leading to severe consequences.
notes: Black-box MCTS fuzzer against AgentDojo and VWAadv; real-world result is misleading agents to navigate to attacker-chosen URLs.

title: Inter-Agent Trust Models: A Comparative Study of Brief, Claim, Proof, Stake, Reputation and Constraint in Agentic Web Protocol Design-A2A, AP2, ERC-8004, and Beyond
evidence_quote: with particular emphasis on LLM-specific fragilities—prompt injection, sycophancy/nudge-susceptibility, hallucination, deception, and misalignment—that render purely reputational or claim-only approaches brittle
notes: Conceptual comparative study of agent-to-agent trust protocols (A2A, AP2, ERC-8004); no experiment, so the consequence is inferred from the stated purpose of gating high-impact actions. Deception between agents could equally be coded reasoning-corruption.

title: Fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs): Improved Prompt Injection Attacks Detection
evidence_quote: These attacks target LLMs applications through using carefully designed input prompts to divert the model from adhering to original instruction, thereby it could execute unintended actions.
notes: Detector trained on the deepset prompt-injection dataset, which is user-supplied prompts, so direct-input. Paper measures only classifier accuracy, never a downstream harm; consequence comes from its own threat description.

title: Owner-Harm: A Missing Threat Model for AI Agent Safety
evidence_quote: the same compositional safety system achieves 100% TPR / 0% FPR on AgentHarm (generic criminal harm, 176 harmful scenarios) yet only 14.8% (4/27; 95% CI: 5.9%–32.5%) on AgentDojo injection tasks (prompt-injection-mediated owner harm)
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the measured gap is on AgentDojo indirect-injection tasks and the motivating incidents (Slack AI credential exfiltration, Copilot calendar injection) are all content-channel attacks. Eight owner-harm categories; Hijacking is the one broken out numerically, but data-exfiltration is heavily represented.

title: ChannelGuard: Safe Models Do Not Compose into Safe Multi-Agent Systems
evidence_quote: Multi-agent LLM applications chain a planner, worker agents, a verifier, and a synthesizer, and every hop between agents is an unmonitored channel through which an adversary can smuggle instructions.
notes: Attack families include tool poisoning and memory poisoning, but the paper's unit of analysis is the inter-agent channel, so multi-agent. Defense deterministically compresses or blocks channel text; the benign-preservation analysis (GSM8K held at 0.867) is where an availability-loss cost would show up, and it does not.

title: HAGE: Harnessing Agentic Memory via RL-Driven Weighted Graph Evolution
evidence_quote: even when long-context models are available, relevant information can be diluted, misplaced, or forgotten as interactions grow, leading to unstable recall and degraded long-term reasoning
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the reported metric is long-horizon QA accuracy over a memory graph, i.e. a wrong final answer with no signal. The paper's own wording ('degraded long-term reasoning') is the counter-argument.

title: Toward Ultra-Long-Horizon Agentic Science: Cognitive Accumulation for Machine Learning Engineering
evidence_quote: By reframing context management as a process of cognitive accumulation, our approach introduces Hierarchical Cognitive Caching (HCC), a multi-tiered architecture inspired by computer systems that enables the structural differentiation of experience over time.
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the degrading content is accumulated execution traces and cross-task experience carried across a 24-hour run, i.e. memory. Metric is MLE-Bench medal rate, which scores the agent's engineering decisions over many cycles, so reasoning-corruption stands. Context-window exhaustion over ultra-long horizons is the stated failure mode, which brushes availability-loss.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Protecting LLM Agents Against Tool Description Poisoning via Isolated Planning
evidence_quote: cross-tool description poisoning can manipulate planner-visible tool metadata to steer an agent's trajectory, even if the poisoned tool itself is never chosen
notes: Explicitly distinguishes itself from tool-output prompt injection: the payload is in the tool description read during planning. Evaluated on AgentDojo and ASB attack success rate.

title: Security-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Post-Quantum Cryptography Intelligence
evidence_quote: there are significant concerns connected with their use in cybersecurity sectors, such as the possibility of hallucinations, vulnerability to rapid injection attacks, and difficulties in confirming the reliability of the sources that are retrieved
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: although the system includes a prompt-injection detector, the quantities actually reported are hallucination rate, confidence score and query accuracy, i.e. wrong final answers. Evidence-based abstention below a 0.4 confidence threshold is a deliberate refusal, not availability-loss.

title: Repair the Amplifier, Not the Symptom: Stable World-Model Correction for Agent Rollouts
evidence_quote: When a rollout fails, repairing the most visible error can leave the underlying error-amplification path intact, while replaying the full graph is expensive and difficult for long-context models to use reliably.
notes: Weak fit for any channel: the corrupted context is the agent's own planning graph (tool calls, validators, memory writes) carried across rollouts, so memory is the closest route; tool-output is arguable since the graph is updated with tool feedback. Consequence is clearly intermediate (rollout error, planning regret).

title: LeakSealer: A Semisupervised Defense for LLMs Against Prompt Injection and Leakage Attacks
evidence_quote: However, retrieved documents may contain classified information such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII). This sensitive data, if compromised, could be exploited by malicious actors for personal gain, such as through unauthorized disclosure or sale
notes: Two evaluation scenarios: jailbreak detection on ToxicChat (direct-input) and PII leakage from RAG context (AUPRC 0.97), which is the headline dynamic result, so RAG + data-exfiltration replaces the original tool-output + goal-hijack.

title: SD-RAG: A Prompt-Injection-Resilient Framework for Selective Disclosure in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_quote: the majority of existing approaches overlook the risks associated with exposing sensitive or access-controlled information directly to the generation model
notes: Defense that sanitizes at the retrieval stage; metric is a privacy score plus resilience to prompt injection that would otherwise override disclosure constraints.

title: ConfusedPilot: Confused Deputy Risks in RAG-based LLMs
evidence_quote: First, we investigate a vulnerability that embeds malicious text in the modified prompt in RAG, corrupting the responses generated by the LLM. Second, we demonstrate a vulnerability that leaks secret data, which leverages the caching mechanism during retrieval.
notes: Two distinct harms are demonstrated and the choice is close: confidentiality (secret data leaked via the retrieval cache, the confused-deputy result the paper is named for) vs integrity (corrupted responses and enterprise misinformation propagation, which is silent-corruption). Kept data-exfiltration.

title: Poisoning the Watchtower: Prompt Injection Attacks Against LLM-Augmented Security Operations Through Adversarial Log Content
evidence_quote: persona hijacks suppress 68% of malicious logs under a naive classifier and remain effective under stronger defenses
notes: Channel is a judgement call: logs are pulled from SIEM/EDR feeds into the model context, which reads as a tool return, though a direct-input coding is defensible since the harness simply builds a prompt from log text. Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the headline metric is suppression of malicious verdicts, i.e. the analyst gets a wrong final judgement with no signal. Summarization injection success (96%) is the goal-hijack-shaped secondary result.

title: Data Extraction Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoors
evidence_quote: When this compromised LLM is integrated into a RAG system, attackers can exploit specific triggers in prompts to manipulate the LLM to leak documents from the retrieval database.
notes: Channel changed from RAG: the attacker's artifact is a poisoned fine-tuned MODEL the victim deploys ('privacy risks associated with the supply chain'), not a retrieved passage; the retrieval database is the victim asset, not the route. Measured harm is verbatim/paraphrased document extraction, so data-exfiltration rather than persistence-backdoor.

title: Black-box Optimization of LLM Outputs by Asking for Directions
evidence_quote: We apply our general method to three attack scenarios: adversarial examples for vision-LLMs, jailbreaks and prompt injections.
notes: Attack-optimization method, not a channel study: the three scenarios span cross-modal (adversarial images), direct-input (jailbreaks) and tool-output (agent prompt injection). Coded direct-input because the optimization loop is driven by the attacker's own queries to the model. Consequence likewise spans misclassification (silent-corruption) and injection (goal-hijack); both axes are low confidence.

title: Multi-Route Search and Adaptive Fusion for Power QA with Small Language Model Guidance
evidence_quote: existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks face several main challenges for power-system documents: semantic drift caused by non-standardized industry terminology, increased semantic noise due to fixedwindow segmentation, and knowledge conflicts in the multi-source retrieval context
notes: No adversary; metrics are recall, BERTScore and RAGAS on power-dispatch QA, i.e. answer correctness.

title: You've Changed: Detecting Modification of Black-Box Large Language Models
evidence_quote: LLM updates force downstream developers to constantly adapt their products as these often silent updates can change LLM performance and behavior
notes: Track changed to Both: the primary phenomenon is non-adversarial (a vendor silently swapping or quantizing the API model behind a developer's product), but the paper also applies the same detector to prompt injection attacks. The dependency is on an upstream model the application consumes, hence supply-chain.

title: SentinelAgent: Graph-based Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
evidence_quote: they also face multi-faceted risks across prompt manipulation, unsafe tool usage, and emergent agent miscoordination
notes: Detection framework over MAS execution graphs; threats span prompt injection, unsafe tool use and multi-agent collusion, so the channel is a dominance call, but the unit of analysis is inter-agent edges and paths. Validated qualitatively on two case studies (email assistant, Magentic-One), no ASR numbers.

title: Evaluating Privilege Usage of Agents with Real-World Tools
evidence_quote: It enables flexible attack injection, either randomly or at specified stages, emulating real-world prompt injection attacks embedded in external content.
notes: Channel changed from tool-metadata: payloads are injected into the content returned by real MCP servers mid-trajectory, not into tool descriptions read before calling. 84.8% ASR on privilege misuse; harms include information leakage (16% workspace tampering), so data-exfiltration is a secondary measured outcome.

title: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
evidence_quote: This threat is further amplified for screenshot-based web agents, which operate on rendered visual webpage rather than structured textual representations, making predominant text-centric defenses ineffective.
notes: The injection only reaches the agent through a rendered screenshot, which is what makes text-centric defenses fail; cross-modal is the defining property of the paper.

title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
evidence_quote: IPIs are embedded within retrieved content (e.g., emails, web pages). Because LLMs fundamentally conflate instructions with data, these malicious payloads can easily hijack the agent's decision-making process, forcing it to execute unauthorized actions (tool calling)
notes: AVAILABILITY-LOSS appears as an explicitly measured secondary axis: the paper's motivation is that existing filter/refusal defenses cause over-refusal that 'prematurely terminates valid agentic workflows', and it reports Utility-under-Attack alongside ASR (over 50% task utility gain).

title: [Short Paper] Forensic Analysis of Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
evidence_quote: adversaries plant crafted malicious prompts that deceive LLMs into generating outputs designed to bypass intended agent functionality, when processed by the associated model
notes: Short forensics paper: generates agent execution logs on an IPI benchmark and tests 12 LLMs as log analysers. The injected content arrives through the agent's tool interactions with the environment.

title: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
evidence_quote: since the data is usually from an external resource, an attacker can manipulate it such that an LLM-Integrated Application returns an attacker-desired result to a user
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: the benchmark covers 7 NLP tasks where the contaminated 'data' (e.g. an applicant's resume text) is concatenated into the prompt by the application, not returned by a tool the model called. The canonical example is the attacker-supplied resume, i.e. an upstream input.

title: Demystifying RCE Vulnerabilities in LLM-Integrated Apps
evidence_quote: Frameworks like LangChain aid LLMintegrated app development, offering code execution utility/APIs for custom actions. However, these capabilities theoretically introduce Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, enabling remote code execution through prompt injections.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: exploitation is 'prompt-based', i.e. the attacker talks to the deployed app directly to steer LLM output into the vulnerable code-execution sink. Consequence changed from data-exfiltration to goal-hijack: the measured result is RCE on 17 apps (13 CVEs); user data leakage and output hijacking are listed as downstream consequences of the RCE.

title: Adaptive Multi‑Layer Framework for Detecting and Mitigating Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models
evidence_quote: Prompt injection attacks are methods that exploit the instruction-following nature of fine-tuned large language models (LLMs), leading to the execution of unintended or malicious commands.
notes: Detector evaluated on a balanced set of 1,405 adversarial and 1,500 benign user prompts; only classification metrics are reported, so the consequence comes from the paper's threat description rather than a measured harm. The framework's own latency/overhead concern is the only availability angle.

title: Prompt Attack Detection with LLM-as-a-Judge and Mixture-of-Models
evidence_quote: Prompt attacks, including jailbreaks and prompt injections, pose a critical security risk to Large Language Model (LLM) systems.
notes: Production guardrail for Singapore public-service chatbots; data is benign chatbot queries plus automated red-teaming adversarial prompts, all user-channel. No downstream harm measured, only detection quality and latency; false positives on benign queries would be the availability cost.

title: AgentSwing: Adaptive Parallel Context Management Routing for Long-Horizon Web Agents
evidence_quote: the agent may fail to reach a stopping point within the allowed resources, or it may
notes: AVAILABILITY-LOSS is a primary measured axis here, not a side effect: the paper formally decomposes long-horizon failure into search efficiency (reaching a stopping point before context budget and max turns are exhausted) and terminal precision (final answer correct). Silent-corruption is the co-equal second axis. Channel changed from direct-input: the accumulated context being managed is search results and visited pages returned by the agent's browsing tools.

title: Defense Against Prompt Injection Attack by Leveraging Attack Techniques
evidence_quote: These attacks trick LLMs into deviating from the original input instructions and executing the attacker’s instructions injected in the data content, such as retrieved results from search engines.
notes: Covers both direct and indirect prompt injection, but the running example and evaluation setting is injected content in retrieved/tool data. Defense inverts attack techniques; utility on clean tasks is reported alongside ASR.

title: Systematization of Knowledge: Security and Safety in the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
evidence_quote: We analyze the structural vulnerabilities of MCP primitives, specifically Resources, Prompts, and Tools, and demonstrate how ”context” can be weaponized to trigger unauthorized operations in multi-agent environments.
notes: Channel set to none: this SoK spans at least five routes by design - Resources (tool-output/RAG), Prompts (direct-input), Tools (tool-metadata/tool poisoning), MCP server distribution (supply-chain) and multi-agent delegation - and no one of them dominates. tool-metadata was the original coding and is the single best guess if a label is forced. Consequence also spans unauthorized actions and epistemic hallucination.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models: A Survey of Attack Methods, Root Causes, and Defense Strategies
evidence_quote: Our findings reveal a swift progression from simple direct injections to sophisticated multimodal attacks, achieving over 90% success rates against unprotected systems.
notes: Channel set to none: a 128-study systematic review covering direct injection, webpage-based indirect injection, memory injection (the ChatGPT long-term-memory spyware case) and multimodal attacks - four-plus routes with no dominant one. direct-input was the original coding.

title: Overeager Coding Agents: Measuring Out-of-Scope Actions on Benign Tasks
evidence_quote: We call these scope expansions overeager actions, an authorization problem distinct from capability failures, prompt injection, or sandbox escapes.
notes: Track changed to ML/AI: the paper explicitly separates itself from prompt injection and studies BENIGN user requests; no adversary is modelled. Channel is direct-input because the manipulated variable is the user prompt (stripping the consent declaration raises the overeager rate 0.0% -> 17.1%). Consequence kept as reasoning-corruption - the agent pursues the goal it was given (tidy the directory) but decides wrongly about scope - though goal-hijack is defensible since it takes actions it was never authorized to take.

title: IPIGuard: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: when interacting with untrusted data sources (e.g., fetching information from public websites), tool responses may contain injected instructions that covertly influence agent behaviors and lead to malicious outcomes, a threat referred to as Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI)
notes: AgentDojo evaluation; the defense constrains tool invocation via a planned dependency graph, and the paper reports the utility cost of that constraint alongside ASR.

title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
evidence_quote: retrieved memories are passed to the LLM without meaningful filtering or prioritization, forcing the model to reason over both relevant and irrelevant content, which makes it prone to distraction by noise
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: evaluation is LoCoMo question answering, where the failure is a wrong final answer. The paper's own framing (distraction while reasoning over noisy memory) supports the original coding, so this axis is contestable.

title: Caught in the Act(ivation): Toward Pre-Output and Multi-Turn Detection of Credential Exfiltration by LLM Agents
evidence_quote: LLM agents often place sensitive credentials in the same context window as untrusted retrieved content, creating a direct path for indirect prompt injection to induce credential exfiltration.
notes: Defense prototype (activation probes, honeytokens, multi-turn leakage budget). Channel is untrusted retrieved/tool content; the measured asset crossing the boundary is credentials.

title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
evidence_quote: Our study shows that existing memory systems underperform because they fail to capture causal and objective information and rely heavily on lossy similarity-based retrieval.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: AMA-Bench scores QA accuracy over agent trajectories (57.22% for the proposed system), i.e. wrong final answers. The memory content is agent states, actions, observations and tool outputs, so tool-output is a partial alternative channel.

title: OPENCLAW-SRT: Resource-Aware Autonomous Agent Architecture for Smart City Edge Computing
evidence_quote: the Supply Chain Risks inherent in unvetted third-party skill stores like ClawHub allow malicious actors to gain system control through reverse shells, further complicating the trust model of autonomous agents
notes: Consequence changed from resource-abuse, which was a misreading: the $1,000/month figure is the owner's own legitimate API bill that the routing layer reduces, not spend on an attacker's behalf, so nothing here is resource-abuse. The only quantified security result is intercepting 99.2% of 'supply chain attacks' originating in third-party skill packages, hence skill (supply-chain is the near-equivalent alternative). IPI via web/email leading to SSH key leakage is a second, unquantified vector.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
evidence_quote: malicious data, embedded within content processed by the LLM, manipulates the model’s behavior to perform unauthorized or unintended actions.
notes: Design-pattern paper; the patterns deliberately restrict agents from solving arbitrary tasks, and the paper discusses that utility cost explicitly. Harms named include data exfiltration, privilege escalation and RCE, all downstream of the hijack.

title: CoMAI: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Robust and Equitable Interview Evaluation
evidence_quote: LLM-based systems remain highly vulnerable to prompt injection attacks [17], owing to blurred boundaries between task instructions and user-provided input. This creates substantial risks in high-stakes assessment contexts.
notes: Channel changed from multi-agent: the architecture is multi-agent but the injection route is the interview CANDIDATE's own typed response, i.e. user-provided input. Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption to silent-corruption because what is measured is scoring accuracy (90.47%) - a wrong final assessment the interviewer cannot see through; goal-hijack is arguable if one reads the injection as the candidate commandeering the scorer. Low confidence on both axes: the paper asserts 'full protection' without reporting an ASR.

title: SpaMEM: Benchmarking Dynamic Spatial Reasoning via Perception-Memory Integration in Embodied Environments
evidence_quote: the sharp collapse from Level 2 to Level 3 exposes a pronounced symbolic scaffolding dependency, where models succeed with text-based bookkeeping but struggle to sustain robust visual memory
notes: Genuinely two channels: Level 2 feeds oracle TEXTUAL state histories (memory) while Level 3 feeds raw egocentric visual streams (cross-modal), and the Level-2-to-Level-3 collapse is the headline, so cross-modal. Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the 15 diagnostic tasks are scored as answer accuracy, not as intermediate decisions.

title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
evidence_quote: BeliefTrack diagnoses three failures: Failed Stay, Failed Update, and Failed Isolation.
notes: One of the clearest reasoning-corruption cases in the batch: symbolic verifiers give exact TURN-LEVEL comparison of the model's intermediate belief state against an oracle, so the measured object really is intermediate state, not a final answer. Task-irrelevant noise arrives in the conversation turns.

title: Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents
evidence_quote: A corrupted or poisoned memory store can silently degrade agent behavior.
notes: Track changed to Both: three of the six motivating problems are non-adversarial (vendor lock-in, session amnesia, coarse access control) while three are adversarial (no integrity verification, injection vulnerability, tampering), and the protocol addresses them jointly. Consequence is inferred, not measured - the only numbers reported are Transfer Continuity Scores (0.83-0.92) - but memory that is serialised and re-hydrated into LATER sessions and other agents is exactly the persistence-backdoor surface.

title: Prometheus: Towards Long-Horizon Codebase Navigation for Repository-Level Problem Solving
evidence_quote: existing agents still struggle to navigate large-scale codebases, as the “Needle-in-a-Haystack” problem persists even with million-token context windows, where relevant evidence is often overwhelmed by large volumes of irrelevant code and documentation
notes: The diluting content is repository files surfaced by exploration and retrieval tools; RAG is a partial alternative since embedding-based codebase retrieval is one of the compared approaches. Consequence stays reasoning-corruption: the stated failure is stateless re-traversal that 'hinders scalable planning and reasoning', measured indirectly through SWE-bench resolution rate.

title: Analysing the Residual Stream of Language Models Under Knowledge Conflicts
evidence_quote: such contextual knowledge can include information that conflicts with the parametric knowledge of the model, which may result in undesired behaviour; for example, the model can rely on inaccurate information sources and produce inaccurate generations
notes: Interpretability study (probing the residual stream) rather than a system; the harm it is trying to pre-empt is an inaccurate generated answer. Note the probe detects conflict BEFORE the answer is emitted, which is the paper's argument that the corruption need not stay silent.

title: EHR-RAG: Bridging Long-Horizon Structured Electronic Health Records and Large Language Models via Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_quote: long-horizon EHRs often exceed LLM context limits, and existing approaches commonly rely on truncation or vanilla retrieval strategies that discard clinically relevant events and temporal dependencies
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the four tasks are clinical PREDICTIONS scored by Macro-F1, i.e. a wrong final label. Context-limit overflow forcing truncation is the stated cause, which is an availability-flavoured mechanism, but nothing is measured as a failure-to-finish.

title: Extended to Reality: Prompt Injection in 3D Environments
evidence_quote: an attacker can place text-bearing physical objects in the environment to override MLLMs' intended task
notes: Payload is physically realised text perceived only through camera capture; the attacker's stated goal is to induce the MLLM to perform the injected task.

title: AdversLLM: A Practical Guide To Governance, Maturity and Risk Assessment For LLM-Based Applications
evidence_quote: it features a prompt injection testing ground with a benchmark dataset to evaluate LLMs' robustness against malicious prompts
notes: Governance/maturity framework rather than a measurement paper; it spans prompt injection, data poisoning and privacy. Channel changed from tool-output because the only concrete artifact is a benchmark of malicious USER prompts fed to the model. Both axes are weakly supported.

title: Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models
evidence_quote: limited query construction and candidate filtering often introduce retrieval noise, resulting in unstable answer accuracy
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the paper names the failure 'unstable answer accuracy' and measures F1 on LoCoMo. Latency is a co-primary metric but it is an efficiency figure, not a defense-induced availability loss.

title: Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
evidence_quote: PAN DORA uses maliciously crafted content to influence the RAG process, effectively initiating jailbreak attacks.
notes: Poisoned documents uploaded into a custom GPT's retrieval knowledge base; success is the model producing the prohibited content the attacker asked for (64.3% GPT-3.5, 34.8% GPT-4).
